doc_title: YouTube: How Real Apps Are Built: System Design for the AI Era | Episode 1
title: System Design for AI Applications
content: System designers think about an entire architecture. Adding an AI assistant to the same application changes the architecture. Users start asking about buying laptops for machine learning. The backend might send requests to an AI model, but the model doesn't automatically know the current inventory. Therefore, retrieval, a vector database, or access to the product database might be needed. The AI might also need memory to remember the user's previous conversation. If the AI can perform actions, it can create orders, check delivery status, cancel subscriptions, book something, or send emails. This isn't just a user-backend database anymore. A user, application, AI orchestration layer, model, memory, vector database, tools, traditional database, external APIs, and possibly other AI agents might be involved.
